title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression CI hook and eval-metrics gating
author: Maeva Chen
description:
Motivation: Prevent regressions in model prompt-sets and track quality metrics in CI. This PR introduces a reusable CI hook for the eval-harness that runs prompt-set regression checks and integrates eval metrics (per-prompt and aggregate) into the merge gating flow. The goal is to fail fast on prompt-set quality regressions (drop in evaluation score beyond configurable thresholds) and provide clear diagnostics to engineers so rollbacks or follow-ups are fast.

What this changes: - Adds a new CI hook script (tools/ci/prompt_regression_check.py) that: 1) fetches the canonical prompt-set for the target model and commit 2) runs the eval-harness locally with the configured eval-metrics backend 3) computes diff metrics (accuracy, BLEU-ish scoring for structured prompts, calibration) and compares against thresholds defined in eval-harness/config/thresholds.yaml - Integrates a lightweight eval-metrics reporter (libs/eval_metrics/client.py) used by CI to push per-run stats to our internal metrics ingestion for historical tracking - Adds gating logic to .github/workflows/eval-harness-ci.yml so pull requests will block merge when the prompt regression check reports a failure (soft-fail for drafts and when a special label is present) - Adds docs and runbook (docs/eval-harness/prompt-regression.md) describing intent, ops steps, and how to update thresholds.

Testing done: - Unit tests for prompt_regression_check.py and eval_metrics client (pytest) - End-to-end run in ephemeral CI against a snapshot of canonical prompts; reproduces a known regression and asserts the PR check fails - Manual canary: enabled for a subset of repos (redwood, redwood-docs) for 48 hours to validate labels and soft-fail behavior

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind a feature-flag (eval_ci.prompt_regression_enabled) default=false for main 2) Enable for low-traffic repos for 72 hours; monitor alerting and noise 3) Gradually enable for monorepo redwood after threshold tuning 4) After 2 weeks, flip feature flag on by default and add to branch protection rules

Notes: thresholds.yaml contains conservative defaults. Teams should iterate on local prompt sets and add noise-tolerant comparisons where necessary. Related Linear tasks: ENG-1423 (CI gating), ENG-1722 (eval metrics backend integration).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Looks good overall; please add a brief note describing the threshold units in thresholds.yaml (absolute vs relative).
Maeva Chen (author): Added comments to thresholds.yaml and updated docs to clarify that thresholds are absolute percentage points by default; also added an example comparing two snapshots.
Priya Nair: Can we soft-fail this check for draft PRs and when the label 'skip-prompt-regression' is present? Otherwise this will be noisy during model onboarding.
Maeva Chen (author): Implemented soft-fail behavior and label override. CI workflow updated to short-circuit when label present.
Ethan Brooks: Unit tests look good. I ran the e2e canary and observed one false-positive on templated prompts; added suggestion to canonicalization logic.
Maeva Chen (author): Tweaked canonicalization and added normalization steps to reduce false-positives. Re-ran canary; noise reduced to acceptable levels.
release_notes:
- Add prompt-set regression CI hook to eval-harness with gating support
- Integrate eval-metrics reporting to CI for historical tracking and alerting
- Configurable thresholds in eval-harness/config/thresholds.yaml (conservative defaults)
- Docs and runbook for teams to onboard their prompt sets
notes_for_oncall: If the prompt-regression CI check starts failing at scale, check metric ingestion rate (eval-metrics service) and thresholds.yaml recent edits. Run the CI job locally using tools/ci/prompt_regression_check.py with the failing snapshot from ci/fixtures/canonical_prompts/.
